subject: tu:game/game/gamemain
value:
RESOLUTION of finding (b) of claim.SP_string-blob-extern-roster-21-tus-364-sites-zero-foreign-blockers.20260904.v1, which asked which of enemy.c / gauntworld.c / gamemain.c is 'reading strings it cannot own'. The answer is NONE of them: every extern is faithful and the defect is one layer down. src/game/game/gamemain.c is currently holding a block of ENEMY.OBJ functions at the bottom of its .text run and a block of gauntworld.obj functions at the top, because the config/GUNE5D/splits.txt .text boundaries are in the wrong places. INVESTIGATION ONLY, no edits: game/game/gamemain and game/enemy/enemy are claude-fleet-worker-PJ's this run.

MECHANISM. Per claim.law.BE_a-string-blob-conversion-reproduces-the-target-only-when-the-tus-whole-rodata-prefix-is-emitted-from-source.20260904.v1, MWCC materialises ONE base per function from its OWN TU's .rodata section and offsets from it, so a function's blob BASE ADDRESS identifies its TU's .rodata section start. The three bases the roster found are therefore three section starts, and they partition the region cleanly: 0x80112370 = enemy's, 0x80112538 = gamemain's, 0x80112788 = gauntworld's. Sorting gamemain.c's 63 blob sites by base gives 17 sites on 0x80112370, 27 on 0x80112538 and 19 on 0x80112788 — three groups, not one file's strings.

CORROBORATION FROM THE XBOX PDB, independent of the base evidence. Mapping every GC .text symbol in 0x8004F800..0x80058200 to its PDB module (research/xbox_symbols/functions_by_module.txt) gives, inside gamemain's declared run 0x80050054..0x80058078: ENEMY.OBJ — init_enemy_vars 0x80050054, format_brain 0x80050394, SetEnemyObj 0x80050618, AllocEnemy 0x8005094C, LoadEnemy 0x80050B8C, GetEnemyType 0x80050FB0, EnemyTypePrefix 0x80051F64, EnemyTypeDesc 0x80051FA0, EnemyDescType 0x80051FDC (plus the unnamed fn_800508A0/fn_80050910/fn_80050DD8/fn_800510A4/fn_80051164/fn_800511D0/fn_80051480/fn_80051568/fn_800516F8/fn_80051C78/fn_80051E1C/fn_8005207C/fn_800520C8 interleaved among them); GAMEDEFS.OBJ — default_options 0x800520CC; gauntworld.obj — FindWobjWanim 0x80055CB8, DoWorldAnimation 0x80055D08, WorldObjectExplode 0x80055E04, WorldExplosion 0x80055E60, world_update 0x8005674C, PrintWorldMemSizes 0x800575CC, GetEnemyTypes 0x8005773C, GetEnemySubtype 0x80057978, InLevel 0x800579E0, LevelLetter 0x80057A6C, LevelItemDesc 0x80057AB4, WorldItemDesc 0x80057AC0, FindWave 0x80057B30, NextAttractWave 0x80057C14, PrevWorldLevel 0x80057D94, NextWorldLevel 0x80057E6C (plus fn_80055F68/fn_8005636C/fn_80056698/fn_80057024/fn_80057ACC/fn_80057BC8/fn_80057F44). The genuinely GAMEMAIN.OBJ block is do_stats_display 0x800522E8 .. fn_80055AFC 0x80055AFC. The two evidence sources agree row for row: every function reading base 0x80112370 is PDB-ENEMY.OBJ, every function reading base 0x80112788 is PDB-gauntworld.obj, every function reading base 0x80112538 is PDB-GAMEMAIN.OBJ.

THE ONE CONTRADICTION, and it must be resolved before anything is moved: init_next_level 0x8005638C is PDB-GAMEMAIN.OBJ but sits between two gauntworld.obj functions in .text AND reads base 0x80112788 (gauntworld's section) at its 17 converted literal sites — see attempt.SP_init-next-level-blob-extern-replaced-by-real-literals-str-pool-refuted-recolor-remains.20260904.v1, whose immediates 16/28/40/... are relative to 0x80112788. Two readings: (i) the GC symbol is a positional mis-adoption of GAMEMAIN.OBJ's local init_next_level (the symaudit spelling_mismatch class; the GC symbol is scope:local) and the function is really gauntworld's, which is what BOTH the .text position and the base symbol say; or (ii) the PDB assignment is right and the base evidence has an exception. Reading (i) is supported 2:1 and reading (ii) would falsify the base-per-section law.

WHAT A FIX REQUIRES, in order. (1) Resolve init_next_level. (2) Move the two .text boundaries in config/GUNE5D/splits.txt: enemy/gamemain from 0x80050054 up to the first true GAMEMAIN.OBJ function (candidate 0x800522E8 do_stats_display, but default_options 0x800520CC is GAMEDEFS.OBJ and must be settled first — there is no game/*/gamedefs.c in the tree, so it is either a mis-adopted name or an unsplit fourth TU); gamemain/gauntworld from 0x80058078 down to 0x80055CB8 (FindWobjWanim), subject to (1). (3) Physically relocate the function bodies between src/game/enemy/enemy.c, src/game/game/gamemain.c and src/game/world/gauntworld.c PRESERVING SOURCE ORDER, because source order is what MWCC's .rodata first-use order and its anonymous-pool numbering follow. (4) Only then declare a `.rodata` run per TU in splits.txt and convert the blob externs to real literals: the ml_mem pilot (attempt.BE_ml-mem-string-blob-becomes-17-real-literals-and-the-rodata-run-matches-end-to-end.20260904.v1) proves the conversion reproduces both the addressing and the data bytes byte-for-byte, but only when the whole prefix is emitted from source, which is exactly what steps 2-3 make possible and what nothing short of them does.

PAYOFF, measured from the image: three currently-unclaimed .rodata runs — enemy 0x80112370..0x80112538 (0x1C8 B), gamemain 0x80112538..0x80112788 (0x250 B), gauntworld 0x80112788..0x80112A9C+ (0x314 B and up) — become claimable Data, and 63 of gamemain's blob sites plus enemy's 3 and gauntworld's 3 stop being fakematches. COST AND RISK: three TUs' anonymous pools renumber at once; gamemain carries four webfrank pins (fn_80054E78, DoWorldAnimation, fn_80051480, fn_800511D0) and DoWorldAnimation is itself in the gauntworld block, so its pin moves TU; every relocated function's register allocation is re-derived from a new declaration context. This is a multi-run structural project with an integrator-level plan, not a lane item, and it is the reason gamemain.c declares no .rodata run today.

SECOND INSTANCE, DIFFERENT ROOT CAUSE, found by the same base-per-section test and reported here because the integrator will meet it next: game/sound/sounds_evt.c and game/sound/sounds.c BOTH materialise base lbl_80114A48. sounds_evt.c's AudioSetupBossStreams reads +348..+512 (0x80114BA4..0x80114C60) and sounds.c's AudioBuildMusicName reads +692..+756 (0x80114CFC..0x80114D24), and the base is not a source artefact on either side: `python tools/gdl/fnasm.py game/sound/sounds AudioBuildMusicName` shows the TARGET at `18: lis r4,0 @lbl_80114A48(ADDR16_HA)` / `1c: addi r30,r4,0 @lbl_80114A48(ADDR16_LO)`, and the same tool on game/sound/sounds_evt AudioSetupBossStreams shows the target at `3c/40` on the identical symbol. But this is NOT a misassigned block: AudioBuildMusicName sits at 0x800A1614, 0x1574 bytes inside sounds.c's declared .text run 0x800A00A0..0x800A18E8, so no boundary move can transfer it while keeping either TU contiguous. The Xbox PDB settles it: `grep '^== .*[Ss][Oo][Uu][Nn][Dd]' research/xbox_symbols/functions_by_module.txt` returns exactly ONE game sound module, `.\Release\SOUNDS.OBJ` at line 2999, and no sounds_evt module at all (neither AudioSetupBossStreams nor AudioBuildMusicName is a PDB name — both are invented GC symbols). So sounds_evt.c and sounds.c are ONE object split into two source files, which is why they share one .rodata section base and why nothing is wrong with either extern. CONSEQUENCE: those 25 blob sites (19 + 6) are unconvertible for as long as the two files compile to two objects — each would emit its own .rodata section and re-base its own immediates, which is exactly the measured failure in attempt.BE_sounds-evt-boss-stream-blob-conversion-rebases-the-pool-and-regresses.20260904.v1. The repair here is a MERGE (one Object entry in configure.py, one .text run in splits.txt, sounds_evt.c's functions first), not a boundary move. FALSIFIER for this paragraph: if the GC .text runs 0x8009C2CC..0x800A00A0 and 0x800A00A0..0x800A18E8 sum to something other than SOUNDS.OBJ's Xbox .text size, or if a second sound module turns up in a re-dumped PDB, the one-object reading is wrong and this reverts to an open misassignment.
